thread.title: Facebook: Opportunity in disaster – Money Junto

title: Facebook: Opportunity in disaster – Money Junto
text:
Facebook’s ( $ FB ) second quarter earnings call was a disaster due to future guidance We believe the negative guidance was intentional and an effort to reset investor expectations The guidance was an investors worst nightmare lower revenues, increased spending and weaker margins Despite the terrible earnings report we think that this is a huge overreaction and opportunistic transitory period for the company Facebook’s social media platform is second to none with plenty more room for additional avenues of monetization The perfect storm = Unreasonable expectations coupled with extremely negative sentiment
Facebook has been plagued with scandal after scandal throughout the past couple of years yet investor expectations remained constant. Investors have largely shrugged off the multiple warnings Facebook executives have issued throughout the past few earnings calls where they explicitly stated. Revenues will be lower Substantial increases in spending MAU’s will be impacted by the GDPR & content delivery
The market worried that at some point the recent controversies and changes impacting Facebook’s core business would come to fruition; however the last two earnings calls largely put these worries to rest and Facebook continued its upward ascent to new highs. Then yesterday happened. Investors were slapped in the face with reality and now many are assuming the worst is yet to come. At one point Facebook was down over 24% in after-hours trading. If Facebook closes today down more than 20% it would mark the largest ever one-day loss of value for a U.S.-traded company.
Courtesy of Bloomberg.com
Everybody knew the day of reckoning was coming, but nobody thought it would be this bad. Negativity amplified the over exaggeration
The negativity toward Facebook created by the media and politicians only added fuel to the fire. There’s no reason $ FB should end today down more than 20%. Yes, $ FB had a terrible earnings call, but there was also a confluence of negative events that happened throughout the quarter between the GDPR going into effect and non-stop negative media coverage surrounding the recent scandals. We believe that this not only creates an opportunity to buy $ FB at a lower price, but to also buy some of the other tech titans getting sold-off $ NFLX , $ AAPL , $ GOOGL , $ PYPL .
The second quarter was full of uncertainty due to the ongoing trade disputes. Overall the U.S. economy is strong, which has led to a much stronger dollar. This has created a significant headwind for U.S. multinationals due to the YoY strength. Facebook stated forex headwinds as a potential culprit for lower revenues in Q3 & Q4, but we don’t see this as a big problem. In fact we think the dollar will slightly weaken from current levels.
Facebook is going to struggle for the next couple of quarters, but not to the extent the market is pricing in. It is the closest thing to a monopoly in social media, which makes it’s advertising space extremely valuable. There is no company even close when it comes to social media market share and people are addicted to social media. There’s no telling where the bottom sets in this year, but we’re optimistic about the long-term outlook, which means extreme weakness should be bought. You may also like
